faqs.a: Enlisted Airmen must be between 17 and 42 years old, following the 2023 increase that raised the maximum enlistment age to 42. Seventeen-year-olds need parental consent. Healthcare and ministry professionals can join up to age 48, and some specialised roles carry different caps, so check your specific career field.

faqs.a: Enlisted Airmen must be US citizens or lawful permanent residents holding a valid Green Card. Officers must be native-born or naturalised US citizens. Foreign nationals cannot enlist from abroad as a route into the United States; residency must already be established before applying.

Most enlisted jobs need an AFQT score of 31 or higher, with technical fields demanding higher line scores. GED holders generally need an AFQT of 65 or more. Your recruiter matches your line scores to the jobs you qualify for.

headline: Join the United States Air Force: Complete 2026 Enlistment Guide
metaDescription: US Air Force recruitment 2026: age 17-42, ASVAB and education rules, MEPS medical screening, 7.5-week BMT at Lackland, plus fitness and body standards.

sections.content:
The United States Air Force enlists Airmen through local recruiters who screen candidates before they attend the Military Entrance Processing Station, known as MEPS. The process typically takes weeks to months, covering initial screening, ASVAB testing, medical and moral evaluations, job selection, background checks and contract signing.

After enlisting, recruits attend Basic Military Training at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland in Texas for seven and a half weeks. BMT builds military discipline, drill, physical conditioning and Air Force heritage, and arrives before technical training school where Airmen learn their specific Air Force Specialty Code.
sections.title: Enlistment Paths and Basic Military Training

sections.content:
Enlisted candidates must be between 17 and 42 years old, with parental consent required at 17. They must be US citizens or lawful permanent residents with a valid Green Card; officers must be native-born or naturalised citizens. A high school diploma or equivalent is required, and GED holders generally need an AFQT score of 65 or higher.

The Air Force uses a body mass index range of 17.5 to 27.5 for body composition. Recruits outside that range take a body fat measurement, capped at 26 percent for males and 36 percent for females. Waivers exist for some medical and moral disqualifiers.
sections.title: Eligibility: Age, Citizenship and Education

sections.content:
Most enlisted jobs require an Armed Forces Qualification Test score of 31 or above, with line scores matched to each Air Force Specialty Code's demands. Technical career fields such as cyber, avionics and intelligence require significantly higher composite scores.

At MEPS, candidates complete the ASVAB, a full medical examination, and a background and moral screening. Job availability depends on Air Force needs, ASVAB scores, physical qualifications and security clearance eligibility, so popular technical jobs fill quickly and flexibility helps.
sections.title: ASVAB Scores and MEPS Screening

sections.content:
Airmen must pass a fitness assessment built around push-ups, sit-ups and a 1.5-mile run, scored against age- and gender-adjusted tables. Arriving at BMT already able to pass makes the seven-and-a-half-week course far easier, since physical training is progressive and cumulative.

Body composition standards apply throughout a career, not just at enlistment. Annual fitness assessments and periodic body composition checks mean staying in shape is an ongoing requirement, with waivers and retests available for temporary medical issues.
